top_signals.title: Iranian Ship Attacks Threaten Middle East Oil Exports as Tanker Traffic Slows
top_signals.summary: A surge in Iranian drone attacks on commercial ships appears to be weighing on Middle Eastern energy exports through the Strait of Hormuz, with 24 attacks reported so far this month. The latest reports from Wednesday morning indicate that two Emirati container ships were struck and sank in the narrow waterway. UBS energy expert Henri Patricot told clients on Wednesday that crude and petroleum-product flows exiting the Gulf of Oman dropped to 9.1 million barrels a day over the past couple of days. top_signals.why_it_matters: Geopolitical escalation affecting commodities, shipping and cross-asset volatility.

top_signals.title: Golden Dome Is Technologically and Financially Infeasible
top_signals.summary:

top_signals.title: IMF Warns of Worldwide Fallout as Attacks on Saudi Arabia Escalate
top_signals.summary: Strikes on Saudi infrastructure by the Yemeni Houthis could affect the global economy, the managing director of the International Monetary Fund has warned. Speaking at a joint event with the World Bank in Thailand, Kristalina Georgieva said that despite this danger, Saudi Arabia remains resilient and has a better economic outlook than most of its neighbors thanks to its diversification efforts in recent years as it aimed to reduce the share of oil revenues in its budget. top_signals.summary: The International Energy Agency said that members agreed to complete the release of 100 million barrels of oil that are still outstanding from an intervention in March aimed at calming global markets.
